rv.q: It’s an exhilarating performance, a work of actorly alchemy.
Purohit's Off Broadway debut is an intriguing but unsatisfying mishmash of melodrama and magical realism.
Awoye Timpo’s fluid production is not to be missed, and its ghosts will haunt you after the lights go down.
Director Awoye Timpo extracts uniformly excellent performances from his cast, bringing a naturalistic authenticity to the proceedings.
Elyria takes an oft-told tale and gives it an original spin.
Elyria feels like a work in progress, its potential as yet unmet.
Ambition is a great thing in a playwright but, in the case of Elyria, Deepa Purohit's reach exceeds her grasp...
It is an ambitious attempt, but ultimately experimental theatrics get in the way of a potentially good story.
There are compelling scenes and uniformly winning performances from the cast, yet the show is frustratingly uneven, adding up to less than the sum of its parts.

cn.t: Purohit's ambitious multi-generational melodrama about Gujarati immigrants offers cultural specificity and strong performances, particularly from Bhavesh Patel, but struggles with uneven storytelling and too many tangled plotlines.
